name: Cryptic crossword No 22,283
preamble: Solutions to the six asterisked clues are of a kind and have no definition.

clue.text: Capital members' gardens redeveloped for the Millennium

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a place, not a noun

blocks.note: Cardiff is the capital of Wales
arms are limbs, members of the body
a park is a public garden

explanation.surface: Members of a capital city's council have their gardens rebuilt for the year 2000 celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardiff Arms Park was the Welsh national rugby ground; it was rebuilt as the Millennium Stadium, opened in 1999 for the Rugby World Cup.
explanation.definitionFit: The old Welsh rugby stadium was demolished and replaced by the Millennium Stadium on the same site, so the description identifies it.

clue.text: Raider starting to arrange a murder most foul

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
something made foul is fouled up and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the first letter of this word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A raider sets out to arrange a particularly foul killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murder most foul' is the Ghost's phrase from Hamlet, which disguises the anagram signal; 'arrange' looks like an anagram indicator but only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A marauder roams about looking for plunder, which is exactly what a raider does.

clue.text: A novel shovel

blocks.note: first meaning: a new exclusive news story, something novel
second meaning: a short-handled tool for lifting loose material

explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a noun meaning a book, but here it is the adjective 'new', and an exclusive new story is the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists call an exclusive story a scoop, and the same word names a spade-like utensil for digging out flour or ice cream.

clue.text: Suited for night warfare, by the sound of it

definitions.text: Suited for night warfare, by the sound of it

blocks.note: surface reading: dressed for fighting in the dark
setter's reading: 'night' heard as 'knight', so suited means wearing a suit of plate for a knight's combat

explanation.surface: Kitted out for a battle fought after dark, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'night' and it could be 'knight'; a knight's suit is a suit of armour.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediaeval knights fought clad in metal plate suits, so a suited knight is protected by armour.

clue.text: In Aqaba, a lime grove houses fertility gods

indicators.note: a building houses what lives inside it, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the run of letters spans the end of the port's name, the article and the start of the fruit
surface padding completing the picture of the orchard

explanation.surface: A citrus grove in the Jordanian port of Aqaba is home to pagan idols.
explanation.walkthrough: Aqaba is Jordan's Red Sea port, and BAALIM is the Hebrew plural of Baal.
explanation.definitionFit: Baal was a Canaanite deity of rain and crops; the Hebrew plural names the many local versions worshipped.

clue.text: * Bridge opponents found after both run away

indicators.note: letters that go away scatter and come back in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
North and East sit next to each other at the card table and play against each other

explanation.surface: Two players flee and their bridge opponents are found once they have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The asterisked answers are Guardian crossword setters; Bunthorne, named after the poet in Gilbert and Sullivan's Patience, was one. In bridge, North partners South and East partners West.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble supplies the definition: each starred answer is the pen name of a Guardian compiler, as Bunthorne was.

clue.text: * Car behind empty garage

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the outside letters
one thing behind another follows it, giving the order of the parts

blocks.note: the first and last letters of this word
the Mini is a classic small British car

explanation.surface: A car parked behind a garage with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Gemini is another Guardian setter's pen name, defined only by the preamble.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble supplies the definition: Gemini is the pseudonym of one of the paper's crossword compilers.

clue.text: A different way of asking to be wed at the bar

blocks.note: a pub's bar is its counter, where drinks are served
asking someone to wed is a proposal of marriage

explanation.surface: Someone pops the question in an unusual setting, propping up the pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay places a marriage offer at the bar, so the bar's serving surface comes first and the offer follows.
explanation.definitionFit: In negotiation an alternative offer made in response to someone else's is called by this compound noun.

clue.text: * Song about goldfish (nearly)

indicators.note: nearly all of something is short of its full length, so the final letter goes
to go about something is to surround it, so one part wraps around the other

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold, and a carp is a fish, here losing its final letter
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A tune about goldfish, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goldfish' has to be split into two words. Araucaria, the monkey puzzle tree, was the pen name of John Graham, the Guardian's best-loved setter.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble supplies the definition: Araucaria was the pseudonym of a famous Guardian crossword compiler.

clue.text: Assured of keeping rust in plants

indicators.note: what one keeps is held within, so the letters lie inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the second

explanation.surface: Someone is told for certain that plants have rust in them.
explanation.walkthrough: UREDO is a botanical term, a stage of the rust fungi that attack cereal crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust is a fungal disease of plants, and this Latin-derived term names that blight or its spore stage.

clue.text: Game needing double top

blocks.note: surface reading: the darts score of double twenty, needed to finish a game
setter's reading: a juggling toy shaped like two spinning tops joined point to point, spun on a string between sticks

explanation.surface: A darts player needs double top to finish the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Double top is the darts term for the double-twenty segment; here it means a double-cone spinning top.
explanation.definitionFit: The juggling game uses a spool like two tops joined at their tips, balanced and spun on a string.

clue.text: Where reluctant Scotsman lives?

definitions.note: the whole clue describes a place

blocks.note: loth means unwilling
Ian is the Scottish form of John, a stock Scotsman's name

explanation.surface: Asking where an unwilling Scot makes his home.
explanation.walkthrough: Lothian is a region of south-east Scotland around Edinburgh, so a Scotsman may well live there.
explanation.definitionFit: The region lies in Scotland, so it is a plausible home for any Scotsman, reluctant or keen.

clue.text: Two notes from a Port-uguese folk song

blocks.note: fa is the fourth syllable of the sol-fa scale
do (or doh) is the first syllable of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A pair of notes taken from a melancholy Portuguese ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'Port-uguese' is a nod to port wine: fado is sung in Lisbon and Porto taverns.
explanation.definitionFit: Fado is the mournful traditional song style of Portugal, often accompanied by guitar.

clue.text: Bouncer at the Leisure Club?

blocks.note: surface reading: a doorman who throws troublemakers out of a club
setter's reading: gym equipment you bounce on, found at a sports centre

explanation.surface: The heavy on the door of a leisure club.
explanation.walkthrough: A bouncer is a nightclub doorman, but also anything that makes you bounce.
explanation.definitionFit: This springy sheet stretched on a frame is used for bouncing exercise in gyms and sports clubs.

clue.text: Good daughters end as good mothers

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: superior means better, of high quality
the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: Well-behaved girls grow up to be fine mothers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a convent the head nun is the Mother Superior, so 'good mothers' are senior nuns in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Superiors are heads of religious houses; a female superior is addressed as Reverend Mother.

clue.text: Silver ring on the floor

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a ring is a round shape

explanation.surface: A silver ring has dropped onto the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The floor here is the sea bed: a vessel touching bottom has run onto it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that strikes the bottom of shallow water is stuck there, resting on the sea bed.

clue.text: It could be bought for a tanner

definitions.text: It could be bought for a tanner

blocks.note: surface reading: priced at sixpence, an old British coin
setter's reading: an ultraviolet appliance purchased for someone who wants a tan

explanation.surface: Something cheap enough to buy for sixpence.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was slang for the old sixpence coin, but here it is a person who tans.
explanation.definitionFit: This ultraviolet lamp gives the skin a bronzed look without sunshine, so someone seeking colour would buy one.

clue.text: Support for the workforce?

blocks.note: surface reading: help or backing for workers
setter's reading: a staff is a stick that supports you, and the workforce is a firm's staff

explanation.walkthrough: A staff is a walking stick, a support, and also the people employed; providing employees is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiring and managing the employees of an organisation is called by this noun.

clue.text: All I do with a potassium compound is this

definitions.text: All I do with a potassium compound is this
definitions.note: the whole clue describes the answer

indicators.note: to compound is to mix ingredients together, so the letters are blended into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A chemist complains that their work consists entirely of potassium compounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a chemical compound; read as wordplay it mixes the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alkaloids are nitrogen-containing plant chemicals such as caffeine and morphine; the clue claims one as a compound.

clue.text: A he-man died horribly here

indicators.note: something done horribly is botched and mangled, so the letters come out disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A muscleman met a grisly end at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here' is the definition: the place where it happened. Maidenhead is a town on the Thames in Berkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue names a location, and this Berkshire town is the place indicated.

clue.text: Where sweethearts fell most violently at sea...

indicators.note: most of something is not all of it, so the tail is dropped
being at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are tossed about

blocks.note: most of the word, losing its final three letters

explanation.surface: Lovers toppled overboard in a violent storm at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweethearts 'fell in love', so the definition is the place they fell into. The ellipsis carries the story on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'fall in love' makes the phrase the state into which a couple tumbles.

clue.text: * ...  then drank the contents

indicators.note: the contents of something are held inside it, so the letters lie within

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Continuing the story: then someone drank what was in the glass.
explanation.walkthrough: Hendra was another Guardian setter's pen name; the preamble defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble supplies the definition: each starred answer is the pseudonym of a Guardian crossword compiler.

clue.text: Orcadian hut for retreating louts

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back the way one came, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: oik is British slang for a boorish lout

explanation.surface: A shelter in Orkney for hooligans on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: Orcadian means from Orkney, the islands off northern Scotland; SKIO is a dialect word found there.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orkney and Shetland dialect this word names a small hut or shed for drying fish.

clue.text: He lives by puffing

blocks.note: surface reading: smoking or panting for breath
setter's reading: someone who earns a living from puffs, exaggerated praise of products

explanation.walkthrough: A puff is an old word for an overblown commendation, the stock in trade of advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who works in advertising makes money writing glowing promotional copy for clients' products.

clue.text: Where one holds the driver!

blocks.note: surface reading: detaining or restraining a motorist
setter's reading: the rear seat of a motorbike, where the passenger clings on to the rider

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the literal sense: the passenger behind a motorcyclist holds on to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The passenger seat behind a motorcycle rider is where a passenger sits, gripping the rider's waist.

clue.text: * Castro, with the heart of a lion

indicators.note: a heart is the centre, so only the middle letters are kept
with means alongside, so the pieces are put together side by side

blocks.note: Fidel Castro, the Cuban leader
the two central letters of the word

explanation.surface: Fidel Castro, said to be as brave as a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: Fidelio, also Beethoven's only opera, was a Guardian setter's pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble supplies the definition: Fidelio is the pseudonym of one of the paper's crossword compilers.

clue.text: * River maiden, perhaps

blocks.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
in cricket a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored

explanation.surface: A girl down by the river, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' looks like a young woman; in cricket it is a scoreless over. Rover is the setter of this very puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble supplies the definition: Rover is the pen name of a Guardian compiler, here signing his own work.

clue.text: Maori chief smuggled gun to IRA

blocks.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, as in gun-running
gat is old American slang for a pistol
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Maori leader ran guns to the Irish Republican Army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smuggled' is past tense here, as in running contraband; 'to' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In New Zealand the Maori word for a tribal leader or noble is this term, still used for respected elders.
